description: Make the monorepo build deterministically in dependency order from clean using TypeScript project references + `tsc -b`, and stop compiling test files in production builds. Then fix the root Dockerfile to build the target backend app via `tsc -b` on a test-excluding build config that pulls in its dependency closure, keeping the OOM fix (no Next.js consoles built). This is the core fix; do it consistently across the whole backend dependency closure.
steps: EDIT FILES VIA BASH ONLY (heredoc/python3) and verify each with `git diff`/`cat` via bash - fs_write does NOT persist to the real disk in this sandbox. After every edit, cat the file back to confirm.

PART A - Add references + build-variant tsconfig to EVERY package in the backend dependency closure. The closure (union of deps of worker, agent-runtime, control-plane-api, transitively) is: domain, config, trust-protocol, contracts, connector-sdk, commerce-graph, policy, observability(only if pulled; NOT required by backends - skip if not in closure), workflow, authorization, evidence, payment-sdk, http-api-kit, merchant-contracts, wallet-* (NOT needed by backends), reference-connector(NOT needed), shopify-connector, razorpay-adapter, data. REQUIRED closure for the 3 backends: domain, config, trust-protocol, contracts, connector-sdk, commerce-graph, workflow, authorization, payment-sdk, http-api-kit, merchant-contracts, shopify-connector, razorpay-adapter, data. Use the @counter/* dependency graph in context.json directory_structure to get each package's direct deps.

For each package/app in the closure, ensure its standard tsconfig.json has a `references` array listing each DIRECT @counter/* dependency as { "path": "../<dep>" } (packages) or { "path": "../../packages/<dep>" } (apps). Mirror the existing style in packages/wallet-application/tsconfig.json. domain/config have no deps so no references. Leave existing correct references (wallet-*, local-mcp) as-is.

For each package/app in the closure, create a sibling tsconfig.build.json with EXACTLY this shape (adjust references to that package's direct deps, pointing to the dep's tsconfig.build.json): { "extends": "./tsconfig.json", "compilerOptions": { "tsBuildInfoFile": "tsconfig.build.tsbuildinfo" }, "exclude": ["**/*.test.ts", "**/*.integration.test.ts"], "references": [ { "path": "../<dep>/tsconfig.build.json" }, ... ] }. For domain/config the references array is empty ([]). VALIDATED spike: this excludes test files AND builds the closure in topological order.

Create tsconfig.build.json for the 3 backend apps too (apps/worker, apps/agent-runtime, apps/control-plane-api), with references pointing to ../../packages/<dep>/tsconfig.build.json for each direct @counter/* dep, and the same exclude + tsBuildInfoFile.

PART B - Change the `build` script of every package/app in the closure (all closure packages AND the 3 backend apps) from `tsc -p tsconfig.json` to `tsc -b tsconfig.build.json`. Do NOT change `typecheck` (keep `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`) or `test` (`vitest run`). Edit package.json via bash and verify.

IMPORTANT for consistency: do the same references-array-on-standard-tsconfig + tsconfig.build.json + `tsc -b tsconfig.build.json` treatment for ALL tsc-built packages/apps in the repo that are reachable in ANY build (so root `pnpm build` is deterministic end-to-end), i.e. also policy, observability, merchant-policy, merchant-application, evidence, wallet-domain, wallet-contracts, wallet-application, reference-connector, and apps reference-buyer, reference-services, local-mcp. This makes the WHOLE `pnpm -r run build` topologically safe, not just the backend subset. The 4 Next.js consoles (landing, merchant-console, operations-console, wallet-console) keep `next build` - do NOT touch them. Package `ui` and `testkit` have no @counter deps; give them an empty references [] build variant if they have a tsc build script, otherwise leave.

PART C - Fix the root Dockerfile. Replace the build line so it: (1) does NOT build the Next.js consoles (preserve OOM fix), (2) reliably builds the target backend app plus its dependency closure in order. Recommended: `RUN pnpm --filter "$(node -p "require('./${BUILD_TARGET}/package.json').name")..." run build` which resolves the target's package NAME (name filter DOES pull the dependency closure, confirmed) and each package now runs `tsc -b tsconfig.build.json`. Because each app's build is `tsc -b`, even a direct `RUN pnpm --filter <name> run build` would build the closure; prefer the name-filter-with-... form for robustness. Verify the resulting filter selects the backend app + its @counter deps but NONE of the Next consoles.

Keep the Dockerfile CMD working: control-plane-api and agent-runtime have dist/main.js AND dist/index.js; worker's fly.worker.toml runs `node apps/worker/dist/index.js`. The generic Dockerfile CMD `node ${BUILD_TARGET}/dist/main.js` must resolve to a real file for each target. Confirm apps/worker/src/main.ts, apps/agent-runtime/src/main.ts, apps/control-plane-api/src/main.ts all exist and are emitted to dist/main.js by the build (they exist in src). Do NOT change fly.*.toml process commands.

After edits, CLEAN and prove locally before Docker: `find . -name '*.tsbuildinfo' -not -path './node_modules/*' -delete && rm -rf apps/*/dist packages/*/dist` then `pnpm --filter "@counter/worker..." run build` must now PASS with no TS2307 and no TS7006, and apps/worker/dist/index.js + apps/worker/dist/main.js must exist. Repeat for @counter/agent-runtime and @counter/control-plane-api.
acceptance_criteria: From CLEAN, `pnpm --filter "@counter/worker..." run build`, `pnpm --filter "@counter/agent-runtime..." run build`, and `pnpm --filter "@counter/control-plane-api..." run build` each PASS with zero TS2307 and zero TS7006 errors.
No *.test.js or *.integration.test.js files appear in any packages/*/dist or apps/*/dist after a production build (tests excluded).
Each backend app dist contains a runnable dist/main.js (and worker also dist/index.js) after build.
The Dockerfile build step targets the backend app package name + dependency closure and does NOT build any of the 4 Next.js consoles.
`build` scripts changed to `tsc -b tsconfig.build.json` only for tsc-built packages/apps; Next.js consoles keep `next build`; typecheck/test scripts unchanged.
verification: source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22 && find . -name '*.tsbuildinfo' -not -path './node_modules/*' -delete && rm -rf apps/*/dist packages/*/dist && pnpm --filter "@counter/worker..." run build && pnpm --filter "@counter/agent-runtime..." run build && pnpm --filter "@counter/control-plane-api..." run build
test emitted files absent: `! ls apps/*/dist/*.test.js packages/*/dist/*.test.js 2>/dev/null` (should list nothing)
findings: IMPLEMENTED & VERIFIED. All edits made via bash (python3), verified with git diff/cat on real disk (fs_write does not persist here). PART A/B: Applied to all 31 tsc-built packages/apps (build script == 'tsc -p tsconfig.json'); the 4 Next.js consoles (landing/merchant-console/operations-console/wallet-console) were left with 'next build' and untouched. For each: (a) standard tsconfig.json got a `references` array of its DIRECT @counter/* deps ({path:'../<dep>'} for packages, {path:'../../packages/<dep>'} for apps); leaf pkgs domain/config/testkit/ui have no deps so no references (ui had none already -> tsconfig.json unchanged in git). Existing inert references on wallet-domain/wallet-contracts/wallet-application/local-mcp matched my dep map and are now active. (b) created sibling tsconfig.build.json: {extends:'./tsconfig.json', compilerOptions:{tsBuildInfoFile:'tsconfig.build.tsbuildinfo'}, exclude:['**/*.test.ts','**/*.integration.test.ts'], references:[{path:'../<dep>/tsconfig.build.json'}...]} (empty [] for leaves). (c) changed `build` script to 'tsc -b tsconfig.build.json'. typecheck ('tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit') and test ('vitest run') left UNCHANGED. Dep graph taken from context.json and cross-checked against every package.json (matched exactly). PART C: Dockerfile build line changed from the failing PATH filter `pnpm --filter "./${BUILD_TARGET}..."` to NAME filter: RUN pnpm --filter "$(node -p "require('./${BUILD_TARGET}/package.json').name")..." run build. Verified via `pnpm --filter <name>... list` that each backend closure = app + its @counter deps ONLY (worker=12 projects, agent-runtime=9, control-plane-api=7) and contains NONE of the 4 Next consoles -> OOM fix preserved. CMD `node ${BUILD_TARGET}/dist/main.js` unchanged; all 3 apps emit dist/main.js (worker also dist/index.js). fly.*.toml and Next apps' next.config settings NOT touched. VERIFICATION (from CLEAN, tsbuildinfo+dist both deleted): `pnpm --filter "@counter/worker..."|"@counter/agent-runtime..."|"@counter/control-plane-api..." run build` ALL exit 0 with ZERO TS2307 and ZERO TS7006. Zero *.test.js/*.integration.test.js emitted in any dist. Entrypoints present: apps/worker/dist/{main.js,index.js}, apps/agent-runtime/dist/main.js, apps/control-plane-api/dist/main.js. Full `pnpm -r run build` (incl. Next consoles + reference apps) exits 0. CLEAN-DOCKER PROOF: `podman build --build-arg BUILD_TARGET=apps/worker` succeeded (the exact env that failed before); build step ran only tsc -b on 12 selected projects, no next build; image had runnable dist/main.js+index.js. NOTE (out of scope, pre-existing): repo has no .dockerignore, so `COPY . .` copies any host .next/dist into the image, but the image BUILD itself never runs `next build` (log shows only tsc), so the OOM constraint holds. Left the source tree CLEAN (removed all dist/tsbuildinfo) and removed the temp podman image. Did NOT git add/commit/push.
